name: Community playhouse operator and box-office volunteer
scenario: I operate captions from the booth for touring shows with a locked running time. Shows, preflight checks, usher handovers and editing the cue file all appear on the same shift calendar.

tasks.title: Run captions during Radio Cabaret
tasks.description: Operate captions from the first audio cue to blackout for the locked sixty-minute studio recording.
tasks.details: The producer owns the playback clock. Loading the file and closing up are separate tasks.
tasks.completion_note: The audio ran continuously to the programmed blackout.

tasks.title: Load the incoming booth file
tasks.description: Make the visiting show open on the booth Mac, replace two broken font links and run the first cue on the confidence monitor.
tasks.details: Files arrived on a USB drive. The visiting technician will check the final monitor.
tasks.completion_note: The second font family used a different name on the booth Mac.

tasks.title: Hand over the foyer desk
tasks.description: Take the float count and tell the incoming usher which visitors asked for aisle access.
tasks.details: Two groups arriving late need a clear handover.
tasks.completion_note: The usher was already at the desk and had the seat plan.

tasks.title: Operate captions for Shortwave Live
tasks.description: Run the caption faders through the forty-five-minute recorded performance. Stop at blackout.
tasks.details: Public stream follows the master file with no interval.
tasks.completion_note: Hit the final cue at the end of the master track.

tasks.title: Check the booth playback outputs
tasks.description: Open the touring workspace, verify both projector outputs and fix the path to the house loop before doors.
tasks.details: The tour has supplied a cue manifest and an updated video file.
tasks.completion_note: The main display worked immediately. The loop still pointed at last week’s share.

tasks.title: Caption the Quiet Hour recording
tasks.description: Drive captions for the locked fifty-minute audio piece, from the countdown beep to the final silence.
tasks.details: No audience talk afterward. The show clock drives the cue track.
tasks.completion_note: The master file finished on time.

tasks.title: Pick up soup supplies after rehearsal
tasks.description: Collect the reserved grain and broth from the shop next to the venue.
tasks.details: Cut through the alley on the walk home.
tasks.completion_note: There was a short queue at the till.

tasks.title: Test the relay for the Blue House tour
tasks.description: Follow the visiting crew’s booth changeover sheet. Verify the mirror display and restore the house workspace when the test is finished.
tasks.details: Two outputs to test and one media relink. Print the handback line.
tasks.completion_note: Connecting the lobby screen changed the display order. The restore check caught it.

sections.heading: Handoff at the booth
sections.body: The company brings one playback bundle on a thumb drive labeled BH-TOUR. Copy the folder BLUE_HOUSE before opening its workspace. Preserve subfolder names. The main output is the full-stage image; the lobby output repeats closed captions over a plain background. The house confidence screen is independent.

sections.heading: Signal list
sections.body: At the booth, trace each cable to its panel label. Display numbers in the operating system can change when the lobby receiver wakes up. Identify the destination from a test image first.

rows: White cross with BLUE HOUSE in upper left
Open caption line on dark field

sections.heading: Acceptance and handback
sections.body: Run B10, B11 and B12 individually. If the lower third is clipped in the lobby, select the receiver’s native mode before touching the text box. If B10 starts but the image is blank, rebind the tour asset to media/main-cross.png on the copied drive. Put a tick by each successful route and write down any patched link. Return the booth to its opening slide and leave the lobby receiver awake.

sections.heading: Receiver fault example
sections.body: The booth preview can show the correct B11 frame while an extender is still showing a cached image from the previous show. Change B11 to a different test cue and ask the foyer checker for the last two words, then switch back. If neither the new words nor a loss-of-signal card appears, inspect the selected input on the foyer receiver. Keep the production set disarmed during this check.

open_tasks.title: Label the spare caption leads
open_tasks.description: Label two HDMI leads for the booth and put them in the road case.
open_tasks.details: Add the green tape before the labels.

open_tasks.title: Check the foyer seat map
open_tasks.description: Mark six aisle seats on the printed floor plan and leave copies with the ushers.
open_tasks.details: Printer has the current floor plan.

holdouts.title: Operate captions for Sea Glass at 19:00
holdouts.description: Run the caption desk for the public performance of Sea Glass. The master track runs 19:00 to 20:15 without interruption.
holdouts.details: Fixed 75-minute public performance. Preflight and teardown are other entries in the calendar.
holdouts.check: The event clock defines the required attendance; three prior fixed-length shows finished at exactly their scheduled duration. Prediction should remain exactly 75 minutes without borrowing setup overruns.

evaluation.rationale: The event clock defines the required attendance; three prior fixed-length shows finished at exactly their scheduled duration. Prediction should remain exactly 75 minutes without borrowing setup overruns.

holdouts.title: Do the Sea Glass booth preflight
holdouts.description: Use the visiting crew sheet to check the two projector routes, fix any broken path and return the house screens to standby.
holdouts.details: We have the touring media already. Check the lobby output separately.
holdouts.check: Previous visiting-show preflights needed 33/25, 38/30 and 43/35, within a narrow range above the guess. Sea Glass took 37/30. The separate fixed public performance adds zero minutes here.

evaluation.rationale: Previous visiting-show preflights needed 33/25, 38/30 and 43/35, within a narrow range above the guess. Sea Glass took 37/30. The separate fixed public performance adds zero minutes here.

sections.heading: What arrives on the company drive
sections.body: The folder SG_HANDOFF contains a QLab workspace, two test clips, a compressed caption track and a read-only copy of the playback manifest. Work from the booth copy in the house shows folder. Starting the production workspace straight from the drive makes a later relink indistinguishable from a missing asset.

sections.heading: Trace the signal
sections.body: The main picture goes directly from output A to the stage projector. Output B runs through the foyer extender. The booth preview is a confidence view and never substitutes for seeing the foyer screen. Ask the house assistant to stand by the foyer monitor with the printed four-word test phrase.

rows: Sea horizon with fine white frame
Captions over a solid blue field
Entire line reads “glass turns with tide”.
Counter advances with the stage test.

sections.heading: Run the test workspace
sections.body: Arm the test cues one at a time. Record the elapsed counter value at the first matching output, but do not check synchrony by eye from the booth alone. A foyer extender can retain the last good image even after losing its input. Ask the assistant which word is on screen after the change to test card B2.
sections.code:
A1  stills/stage-frame.png  -> A
B1  tests/foyer-blue.mov    -> B
B2  tests/foyer-grey.mov    -> B
H0  house/doors-open.png    -> A

sections.heading: A missing media example
sections.body: A workspace copied from TourMac might still refer to /Volumes/SG_SOURCE/tests/foyer-grey.mov. Select the identically named file in the booth copy. Run B1 and B2 again, check that the filename remains relative after saving, and record which cue needed the change. Never relink a test card to a production caption asset just because the basename looks close.

sections.heading: Release the booth
sections.body: Stop the test cues, select the house standby workspace, put H0 on stage, and return output B to the house welcome screen. Leave the touring workspace on the local disk for the performance operator. Sign the handover with the route that failed, the action taken, and the name of the crew member who checked the foyer.

sections.heading: What to write on the handback slip
sections.body: Record the test asset, the physical destination and the observed far-end result in one line per route. For instance, “B2 / foyer / grey card reached screen, last word changed to tide.” A note that the cue advanced in QLab alone is insufficient. Leave any physical cable moves on the patch list and return the booth to its documented rack labels before releasing it to doors.
